_about: Where jobs come from. Each section maps to an adapter in src/jobhunter/sources/. Any entry or section can take "enabled": false. Keys starting with _ are comments.
_greenhouse_boards: Removed 2026-09-27: these boards' remote roles were US/Canada or single-country only. The greenhouse adapter still exists; add a "greenhouse_boards" list back to use it for a company that hires internationally.

watch_boards._note: After each run, the Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby board of every company with a shortlisted job is found (from the job's own links, else by trying slugs of its name and keeping a board only if it lists the job's title) and fetched from the next run on. Stored in the database, not here: `jobhunter boards` lists them, `jobhunter boards --remove kind:slug` drops one for good. Job sites, agencies and blocked companies are never watched. See src/jobhunter/boards.py.

_gulf_boards: Companies in the UAE, Qatar and Lebanon, on their own careers systems (checked 2026-10-10, docs/research). Their jobs are mostly on-site: the relocation rules in config/filters.json decide. Saudi-only companies are left out.

lever_boards._note: Lever returns 'Document not found' and no Greenhouse/Ashby board exists under this name (checked 2026-09-25). Find their current careers page to re-add.

ashby_boards._note: Moved from greenhouse 'circleso' (404). Verified: the Ashby 'circle' board is Circle.so.
Moved from lever 'kraken123' (empty board). Kraken's jobs are on Ashby now.
Abu Dhabi 'Deployed' AI roles next to its San Francisco ones (2026-10-21 research).

getro._note: Investor (VC) job boards on Getro: only the companies each fund invested in, so no agencies. No descriptions (the API has none). Remote jobs from the big funds; jobs in the UAE, Qatar or Lebanon from the Gulf ones. An id is in a board's page source: "network":{"id":...}. Checked 2026-10-10.

boards._note: European funds and the big ones' EU jobs, for the visa list (checked 2026-10-13). Only the UK, the Netherlands and Ireland: Getro gives no posting text, so a job gets on the list only through those countries' sponsor registers; one that does makes its company's own board watched, and that board's postings have the text.
boards.name: Index Ventures (UK, NL, IE)

arbeitnow._note: Jobs in Germany, the Netherlands and the UK, for the visa list (visa.py). Public API, no key; asks for a link back (the report links each job's Arbeitnow page). visa_sponsorship=true is set per company, not per job, so it only trims NL and UK; Germany is fetched whole and the posting's words decide. Only titles with one of `queries` are kept (most jobs are other roles, and every fetched job is stored). Each site is read newest first until a page reaches jobs older than lookback_hours. ~11 requests a run. Checked 2026-10-13 (docs/research).

workable._note: Workable's public job search: every company on Workable, by country, for the visa list (visa.py). Full descriptions. 20 a page, sorted by relevance, so day_range keeps it to recent postings. One search per query and country: up to queries x countries x max_pages requests (about 21-42). Checked 2026-10-13: 57 of 805 target roles in the seven countries reached the visa list (docs/research).

serpapi._note: Google Jobs (includes LinkedIn postings). Needs SERPAPI_API_KEY in .env; skipped without it. One credit per query page per run (the 21:00 run only). A query with no location searches the US market. 2026-10-19, from the stored results: the Gulf city search gave 15 of the 18 shortlisted and 5 of the 6 applied-to jobs; the six US 'remote' searches gave ~245 results, 4 shortlisted, 1 applied; the trading ones none. Now: each Gulf city every day (search words in turn), Beirut twice a day (a test found 10 jobs no other source had, 3 shortlisted), two remote searches. 7 credits/day, ~217/month (the Free plan has 250).

_remote_api: Remotive was removed 2026-10-21: its free API returns only 10 jobs in total, whatever the parameters.

jobicy._note: Jobicy API: remote jobs with the region each company hires in ('Anywhere', 'EMEA', 'USA'). No key; credit Jobicy and send applications to its job URL (both links are the Jobicy page). Newest first, read until jobs older than lookback_hours. Only titles with one of `queries` are kept. Checked 2026-10-21 (docs/research/2026-10-21-market-size.md).

euremotejobs._note: EU Remote Jobs: remote jobs open in Europe, EMEA or worldwide. The whole list is read newest first (robots.txt blocks its category search) and only titles with one of `queries` get their job page read (full text, allowed countries, the company's apply link). ~100 jobs a day of all kinds. Checked 2026-10-21.

linkedin._note: LinkedIn's logged-out job search (src/jobhunter/sources/linkedin.py). Logged out, only keywords, location and the posted-within window work (no remote or level filter), so searches are by place: the UAE and Qatar (relocation), Lebanon, and UK/NL jobs that mention visa sponsorship (visa list). Each request waits `pause` seconds (about 1/s gets HTTP 429); only titles with one of `queries` get their page read. LinkedIn's terms forbid automated access: used anyway at this low volume, the user's call (2026-10-21). The 2026-10-21 research found UAE fits missing from the DB (Core42/G42, Open Innovation AI, ADG, Al-Futtaim).

himalayas._note: country=LB makes Himalayas return jobs that list Lebanon or list no countries. No countries is treated as unknown, not worldwide. 2026-10-19: the best source (most applied-to jobs) searched only Python/backend words; added the profile's other target roles.

remoteok._note: The API returns its latest ~100 jobs only. 'queries' is a local filter on title + tags.

hackernews._note: Latest 'Ask HN: Who is hiring?' thread.

hiringcafe._note: Not implemented: hiring.cafe blocks automated requests (HTTP 403).

remote100k._note: Not implemented: HTML only, no feed. Categories are /remote-jobs/<slug> (engineering, software-engineer); 'python'/'fastapi' pages do not exist.
